messages.subject: Re: setar() function
messages.body_plain:
Dear Chibsi

I am glad the package can be useful for your thesis! Concerning your
question, you can find the definition in this document:
http://stat.ethz.ch/CRAN/web/packages/tsDyn/vignettes/tsDyn.pdf page 3.
If this is still not clear please let us know so we can improve the doc.

Note that in case of setar, one should use either d/steps or
mL/mH/ML/MH, both together might make it fail. Also, are you aware of
the package tseriesChaos for chaos theory?

I cced to the tsdyn mailing list. You can subscribe to it to ask further
questions, as well as to stay informed about new features. If you use
tsDyn for your master thesis, we would be happy to receive a copy when
finished and, even best, a link to your a permanent location so that we
can reference which papers used our package. For sure, we also
acknowledge when the package is cited also :-)

Hope this helps

Matthieu

Le 05. 09. 10 01:31, chi...@gmail.com a �crit :
> Dear Matthieu,
>
> I am using your package tsDyn in particular the setar() function and I
> am not sure what the parameters (m, d, and steps) are referring to. I
> am fitting the model to a chaotic dynamic process and some of the
> language used to define parameters are the same so I do not want to
> confuse things and make assumptions as to what is being referred to.
> Do I assume that m is the actual embedding dimension of the dynamical
> system, and d is the time delay (e.g. measured from the ACF or the
> average Mutual Information)? Steps is automatically set to equal d,
> should I change this to equal 1 or leave it alone?
>
> I am writing up my MSc thesis on this subject and I would appreciate
> as swift a response as possible.
>
> Kind regards
>
> Chibisi
>

messages.body_plain:
Fabio

as mentioned

# unrestricted threshold:
setar(lynx-mean(lynx), ML=1, MH=1, MM=0, nthresh=2, restriction="none")

this is the version for unrestricted (not symetric threshold). The version for restricted is (corresponding to BAND-TAR):

# symetric threshold:
setar(lynx-mean(lynx), ML=1, MH=1, MM=0, nthresh=1, restriction="OuterSymAll")

the -mean(lynx) is just to ensure there are observations below/above 0. And variables are in level, not diff as you mention.

Hope this helps

Matthieu

messages.body_plain:
I could not see the equation you want to estimate (this mathml thing). Can you either send paper, or write it in Latex like style?

But if your problem is you want
\Delta X_t = \rho X_{t-1} ... you just divide add or remove 1 to the coef you estimated, nothing else. See the vignette for mopre clarification:

You can do it also like this:

# symetric threshold:
setar(lynx-mean(lynx), ML=1, MH=1, MM=0, nthresh=1, restriction="OuterSymAll", type="ADF")

but you have automatically one lag more. It is to date no possible to have only the level on the right hand side.

All this is explained in section 3.1 of manual:
http://stat.ethz.ch/CRAN/web/packages/tsDyn/vignettes/tsDyn.pdf

let me know if it is still not clear!

Hope this helps

Matthieu
